mainTopic: Correcting a parent respectfully; one liable for two court-imposed death penalties, its source in יחזקאל, and רבי יוסי's 'first prohibition' rule
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: a son is taught not to correct his father bluntly. A ברייתא and the גמרא's sharpening of it teach that he should gently mention a פסוק, so the father is not shamed. Then a new משנה teaches that someone liable for two מיתות בית דין receives the more severe one. רבי יוסי disagrees about a single act that carries two death penalties. רבא explains that the משנה's first rule teaches that a man already sentenced for a lighter sin is not treated as 'already dead' if he commits a more severe one. The source for the rule is a פסוק in יחזקאל 18, defended against רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge. The גמרא then brings an אגדה reading of nearby פסוקים about the צדיק, and רבי עקיבא comforts רבן גמליאל that keeping even one of these qualities earns life. Finally, a ברייתא explains רבי יוסי's 'first prohibition' rule with a mother-in-law who is also a married woman. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges it from רבי אבהו's principle of איסור מוסיף, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Do not correct your father that way
steps.stepSummary: A son is told not to speak to his father in the blunt way he just did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't speak to your father like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story from the previous דף, where a son bluntly told his father he was wrong. Here he is taught that this way of speaking is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether the son was right about the law. The issue is how he said it. כיבוד אב requires correcting a parent without disrespect, and the next step brings a source for this.

phrases.english: Do not say it this way to your father,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא לֵיהּ לַאֲבוּךְ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous daf about a son correcting his father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son may not tell his father bluntly that he is wrong.

steps.title: A ברייתא on how to tell a father he sinned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a son should not accuse his father of violating the Torah. Instead he should say, 'This is what the Torah says.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone's father was breaking a Torah law, the son should not say, 'Father, you broke the Torah.' Instead he says, 'Father, this is what is written in the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the instruction in step 1. It teaches a gentle way to point out a father's mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts two ways of speaking. One is a direct accusation ('you sinned'). The other points to the Torah ('this is what is written'). The goal is to inform the father without shaming him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Violating the words of the Torah
So it is written in the Torah

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה אָבִיו עוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: If one's father was violating Torah matters,
he should not say to him:
'Father, you violated Torah matters.'
Rather, he says to him:
'Father, this is what is written in the Torah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the instruction not to correct one's father bluntly.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a son must not bluntly correct his father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the proper way to tell a father he is violating the Torah.

steps.title: Isn't that the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that saying 'this is written in the Torah' still points straight at the father's mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, this is the same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. Its suggested phrase seems just as embarrassing as the forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son says 'this is what the Torah says' right after his father acts, the father hears it as 'you sinned.' The gentle version does not really avoid the shame, so the ברייתא's wording needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as that

phrases.english: In the end, this is the same thing!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording suggested by the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggested phrase 'Father, so it is written in the Torah.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That phrase still clearly tells the father he sinned, so it shames him just as much as the forbidden phrase.

steps.title: Better wording: 'There is a verse in the Torah'
steps.stepSummary: The son should mention the verse in a general way, as if just sharing a פסוק, without tying it to what his father did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he says to him: 'Father, there is a verse written in the Torah, and this is what it says.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting the ברייתא's wording. The son should bring up the verse as general learning, not as a comment on his father's act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is small but real. 'This is written' sounds like a ruling on what the father just did. 'There is a verse that says...' sounds like sharing Torah, and the father can draw the conclusion himself. That protects his dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is / this is how it goes

steps.whatToRemember: When a parent does something wrong, you may inform them, but in a way that does not shame them. You might gently mention a פסוק so they can realize the mistake on their own.

phrases.english: Rather, he says to him:
'Father, there is a verse written in the Torah, and this is what it says.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ: אַבָּא, מִקְרָא כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה כָּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the source so it truly avoids shaming the father.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'this is written in the Torah' is gentle enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son should mention the פסוק generally, without linking it directly to his father's act.

steps.title: משנה: liable for two death penalties
steps.stepSummary: Someone liable for two court-imposed death penalties receives the more severe one. רבי יוסי disagrees about a single act that carries two death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who became liable for two different court death penalties is judged with the more severe one. If he did one sin that makes him liable for two death penalties, he is judged with the more severe one. רבי יוסי says: he is judged by the first forbidden connection that came upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two cases. In the first, a person commits two separate capital sins. In the second, a single act counts as two capital sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the תנא קמא gives the more severe death. רבי יוסי disagrees only in the second case. He says we follow whichever forbidden status was there first. For example, a woman might have been his mother-in-law before she became a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Death penalties imposed by the court
He is judged with the more severe one
Connection / forbidden status that attached to him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. The first is two separate sins. The second is one act that falls under two prohibitions, and רבי יוסי argues only about that second case.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב בִּשְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who became liable for two court-imposed death penalties
is sentenced with the more severe one.
If he committed one sin for which he became liable for two death penalties,
he is sentenced with the more severe one.
Rabbi Yosei says:
He is sentenced according to the first forbidden connection that came upon him.
phrases.notes: He means whichever forbidden status applied first. That one decides which death he gets.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב בִּשְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic, unrelated to the story before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person liable for two court death penalties gets the more severe one. For one act with two death penalties, רבי יוסי says the first prohibition decides.

steps.title: Isn't the first rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say this. Surely a person should not gain a lighter death by adding another sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: That is obvious! Otherwise, should he profit from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's first rule as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone deserves both a light death and a severe death, giving him only the lighter one would mean the extra sin helped him. That makes no sense, so the גמרא asks what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: That is obvious!
Otherwise, should he profit from it?
phrases.notes: He means: should the second sin earn him a lighter death? That would be absurd.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! אֶלָּא, אִיתְּגוֹרֵי אִיתְּגוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה's first ruling needed to be stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's first rule: liable for two deaths, judged with the more severe one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one would think an extra sin should earn a lighter punishment, so the rule seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: already sentenced, then sinned again
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה is about a man already sentenced for a lighter sin who then committed a more severe one. We might have thought he counts as 'already dead,' but he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with? He committed a lighter sin, was sentenced for that lighter sin, and then went on to commit a more severe sin. You might have thought: since he was already sentenced for the lighter sin, this man is as good as dead. The משנה teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question of step 6 by placing the משנה in a specific, less obvious case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might reason that once the sentence is final, the man is legally 'dead,' so new sins don't count. The משנה teaches that the later, more severe sin still counts, and he receives the more severe death.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
A dead man (someone considered already killed)

steps.whatToRemember: A man already sentenced to death for a lighter sin who then commits a more severe capital sin is not ignored as 'already dead.' He receives the more severe death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person under a final death sentence is still responsible for what he does afterward.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where he committed a lighter sin,
and his sentence was finalized for the lighter sin,
and then he went on to commit a more severe sin.
It could enter your mind to say:
since his sentence was already finalized for the lighter sin,
this man counts as a dead man.
So the Mishnah teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 6 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the משנה in a specific case where its ruling is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once he is sentenced for the lighter sin, he is legally 'dead' and later sins don't change anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not considered dead. The later, more severe sin counts, and he receives the more severe death.

steps.title: Where does the 'stricter death' rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The father of רב יוסף בר חמא asks רבה בר נתן for the source of the rule that one liable to two court deaths gets the more severe one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רב יוסף בר חמא asked רבה בר נתן: Where do we learn what the Rabbis said, that someone liable to two court death penalties is judged with the more severe one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the Torah source of the rule we saw in the משנה (step 5). This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5–7 discussed what the rule means and when it applies. Now the question is different: where does it come from? The answer will come from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this matter learned?
Death penalties carried out by the court
He is judged with the more severe one

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: The father of Rav Yosef bar Chama asked
of Rabba bar Natan:
From where is this matter that the Rabbis said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: One who became liable to two court-imposed deaths
phrases.notes: This is the rule from the משנה we just learned in step 5.

phrases.english: is judged with the more severe one?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא מֵרַבָּה בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה's rule to asking for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for giving the more severe death to someone liable to two.

steps.title: The source verse in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר נתן quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל describing a wicked son who commits several sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he begets a violent son, a shedder of blood… he has eaten upon the mountains, and defiled his neighbor's wife… and lifted his eyes toward the idols.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר נתן answers by quoting a פסוק that lists several serious sins done by one person. The next step will explain how this proves the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is that one person here commits several different capital sins. Each sin carries its own death penalty, so the question becomes which death he actually receives.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sheds blood, a murderer

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And he begets a violent son, a shedder of blood, [etc.]
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:10–12. The 'etc.' means the פסוק goes on, and the גמרא skips ahead.

phrases.english: he has eaten upon the mountains
and defiled his neighbor's wife
and lifted his eyes toward the idols."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in יחזקאל 18 about the wicked son.

steps.title: Three sins, three deaths, but one punishment: stoning
steps.stepSummary: Each sin in the פסוק carries a different death (sword, strangulation, stoning), yet the next פסוק gives only stoning, the most severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A shedder of blood' is punished by the sword. 'Defiled his neighbor's wife' means a married woman, punished by strangulation. 'Lifted his eyes toward the idols' means idol worship, punished by stoning. And it is written: 'He shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him', which means stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר נתן explains the proof. The man earned three different deaths, and the פסוק says he gets stoning, the strictest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Murder is punished by the sword, adultery with a married woman by strangulation (חנק), and idol worship by stoning (סקילה). The punishment the פסוק gives is 'his blood shall be upon him,' which means stoning. Since stoning is the most severe of the three, this shows he receives the stricter death.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, the most severe court death
His blood is upon him, the Torah's phrase for stoning

phrases.english: "And he begets a violent son, a shedder of blood": by the sword;
"defiled his neighbor's wife":
this is a married woman, by strangulation;
"and lifted his eyes toward the idols":
this is idol worship, by stoning.
And it is written: "He shall surely be put to death; his blood shall be upon him":
by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״מוֹת יוּמָת דָּמָיו בּוֹ יִהְיֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted פסוק proves the rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one liable to two court deaths receives the more severe one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 18:10–13: three sins with different deaths, punished only by stoning.

steps.title: Maybe all three sins are stoning sins
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק suggests reading every sin in the פסוק as a stoning sin, which would ruin the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged this: Say they are all stoning sins. 'A shedder of blood' is the rebellious son, who is stoned. 'Defiled his neighbor's wife' is a betrothed young woman, which is stoning. 'Lifted his eyes toward the idols' is idol worship, which is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the proof. He reads each sin as one that is already punished by stoning, so the פסוק no longer shows a choice between different deaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked only because the three sins had different deaths. If every sin is a stoning sin, giving stoning is just the normal punishment. Then nothing shows that the stricter death wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way
The wayward and rebellious son, who is stoned
A betrothed young woman; relations with her are punished by stoning

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not arguing with the rule itself. He only says this פסוק does not prove it.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak challenged it:
Say that all of them are by stoning.
"And he begets a violent son, a shedder of blood":
this is a wayward and rebellious son, who is stoned;
"defiled his neighbor's wife":
this is a betrothed young woman, which is by stoning;
"and lifted his eyes toward the idols":
this is idol worship, which is by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק used as proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר נתן's reading that each sin carries a different death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each sin can be read as a stoning sin, so stoning is just the normal punishment and proves nothing about choosing the stricter death.

steps.title: Then יחזקאל would teach nothing new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that under רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading, the פסוק in יחזקאל would add no new lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is יחזקאל teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. If every sin were already a stoning sin, יחזקאל would be telling us nothing we did not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נביא's words are expected to teach something. רבה בר נתן's reading gives a new lesson, that the stricter death wins. רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading leaves the פסוק with no new point.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן יְחֶזְקֵאל?
phrases.english: If so, what is Yechezkel teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pushes the challenger's reading to an unacceptable result: a פסוק with no lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three sins are stoning sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sins must carry different deaths, or יחזקאל would teach nothing.

steps.title: Maybe יחזקאל is just repeating the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that יחזקאל might simply be reviewing laws already in the Torah, without adding anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he is repeating the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A נביא could be reminding the people of Torah laws without teaching anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed יחזקאל must be adding something. This step says that is not necessary, because a נביא may just repeat the Torah to warn the people. If so, רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading could still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: He is repeating, going over again

phrases.english: Perhaps he is repeating the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means יחזקאל might just be reminding the people of laws already written in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא תּוֹרָה קָא מַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind the answer in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that יחזקאל must be teaching a new law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נביא may simply review Torah laws, so a 'no new lesson' reading is not impossible.

steps.title: If he were repeating, he would use משה רבינו's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if יחזקאל were only repeating the Torah, he would have used the same wording as משה רבינו. Since he did not, he is teaching something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should have repeated it the way משה רבינו said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that יחזקאל is only repeating the Torah, and so the proof from the פסוק stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is only reviewing a law would use the Torah's own words. יחזקאל uses different wording ('shedder of blood,' 'his neighbor's wife'), so he must mean to teach something. That brings back רבה בר נתן's reading: the stricter death wins.

keyTerms.meaning: משה our teacher, meaning the Torah's own wording

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that one liable to two court deaths gets the more severe one comes from יחזקאל 18. Three sins with different deaths are punished only by stoning, and יחזקאל's unusual wording shows he is teaching this as a new lesson.

phrases.english: If so, he should have repeated it
the way Moshe our teacher repeated it.
phrases.notes: He means using the same words the Torah uses. יחזקאל's different wording shows he has a new point.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְאַהְדּוֹרַהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאַהְדְּרַהּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback of step 13 and restores the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument from wording: a mere review would copy the Torah's language.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יחזקאל might just be reviewing Torah laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: His different wording shows he is teaching a new law, so the proof for the stricter death stands.

steps.title: A deeper reading of 'not eating on the mountains' and 'not lifting his eyes'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא ברבי חנינא explains the first two phrases of יחזקאל 18:6 as hints to humility and self-reliance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא ברבי חנינא taught: 'He did not eat upon the mountains' means he did not live off the merit of his fathers. 'He did not lift his eyes to the idols of Israel' means he did not walk around with a proud, upright posture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new teaching by רב אחא ברבי חנינא about a nearby פסוק in the same chapter of יחזקאל (18:6), which describes the righteous man. He reads it as a higher level of righteousness, not just avoiding big sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply not worshipping idols is not enough to earn the title צדיק, so the words must hint at something finer. 'Eating on the mountains' becomes living off one's ancestors' merit. 'Lifting eyes to idols' becomes walking with a proud, upright posture.

keyTerms.meaning: He expounded; taught a non-literal reading of a פסוק

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rabbi Chanina expounded:
What is meant by what is written: "He did not eat upon the mountains"?
That he did not eat on the merit of his fathers.
phrases.notes: He means: he did not get by on his ancestors' good name, but on his own deeds.

phrases.english: "And his eyes he did not lift
toward the idols of the house of Israel"?
That he did not walk with an upright stature.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to an אגדה reading of a nearby פסוק in יחזקאל 18 (verse 6, about the righteous man).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first phrases of יחזקאל 18:6 describe a צדיק who relies on his own merit and avoids arrogance.

steps.title: A deeper reading of 'his neighbor's wife' and 'a נדה', and the reward of life
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא ברבי חנינא continues: not harming a friend's business, and not taking from charity, and the פסוק says such a צדיק will live.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He did not defile his neighbor's wife' means he did not move in on his friend's trade. 'He did not come near a נדה' means he did not take from the charity fund. And it says: 'He is a צדיק, he will surely live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same teacher finishes his reading of the פסוק, then quotes the promise that such a person will live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the plain sins are read as hints to finer behavior: cutting into someone's livelihood is like taking what belongs to him, and living off צדקה is avoided even when allowed. The closing פסוק, 'he will surely live', sets up רבן גמליאל's worry in the next step.

phrases.english: "And his neighbor's wife he did not defile" –
that he did not encroach on his friend's trade,
"And to a menstruating woman he did not come near" –
that he did not benefit from the charity fund.
And it is written: "He is a righteous man, he shall surely live."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְאֶת אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ לֹא טִמֵּא״ – שֶׁלֹּא יָרַד לְאוּמָּנוּת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same דרשה on the rest of the פסוק and adds the promise of life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with these refined qualities is called a צדיק who will live.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל cries: only someone who does all of them lives?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל would cry at this פסוק, because it seemed only someone who keeps every item will live.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן גמליאל reached this פסוק, he would cry. He said: Only someone who does all of these will live, but someone who does just one of them will not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל raises a frightening problem: the bar for 'life' seems to be keeping every single item on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry comes from reading the list as one package: you must have all these qualities together. Since few people reach that, the promise of life seems out of reach. It is worded as a cry, but it works as a challenge that the next step will answer.

phrases.english: When Rabban Gamliel would reach
this verse, he would cry.
He said: One who does all of them,
he is the one who lives,
with one of them – not?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַגִּיעַ לְמִקְרָא הַזֶּה, הָיָה בּוֹכֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the promise of life at the end of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The promise 'he shall surely live' in יחזקאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reward depends on doing every item, almost no one can earn it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: even one of them is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא proves from the Torah's phrase 'all of these' about forbidden relations that 'all' can mean 'any one of these'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If so, the Torah says 'Do not become impure with all of these.' Would you say that only someone who does all of them is guilty, but someone who does one of them is not? Obviously, it means with any one of these. So here too: with any one of these.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא comforts רבן גמליאל by showing that the word 'all' does not have to mean 'all together'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one thinks a person is only punished for forbidden relations if he commits every one of them, so 'all of these' there must mean 'any one of these'. רבי עקיבא applies the same reading to יחזקאל: keeping even one of these qualities earns life. The fear is removed by showing a parallel phrase in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introducing a problem with the reasoning)
With any one of all these

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, the promise of life in יחזקאל applies even to someone who has just one of these righteous qualities.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: If that is so,
"Do not become defiled with all of these,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:24, said right after the list of forbidden relations.

phrases.english: is it also so that with all of them – yes,
with one of them – no?
Rather, it means: with one of all these,
so too here: with one of all these.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's worry in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel reading from another פסוק (the word 'all' means 'any one')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a person who does all the listed good deeds will live.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing even one of them earns life, just as 'all of these' in ויקרא means any one.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי's rule of the first prohibition work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and brings a ברייתא asking how רבי יוסי's rule, 'judged by the first prohibition', works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He committed one sin [that carries two death penalties].' A ברייתא teaches: How does רבי יוסי say that he is judged by the first prohibition that came upon him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and sets up a ברייתא that will explain רבי יוסי's opinion with examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the first opinion says that when one act carries two death penalties, the more severe one is used. רבי יוסי says instead that we use the prohibition that applied to the woman first. The ברייתא asks for a concrete case of how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The first bond, the first prohibition that applied

phrases.english: "He violated a transgression."
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה, where one act carries two death penalties.

phrases.english: It was taught: How did Rabbi Yosei say?
He is sentenced by the first prohibition that came upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָבַר עֲבֵירָה. תַּנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה about one act with two death penalties.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear case showing what 'the first prohibition' means in רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: Examples: mother-in-law first, or married woman first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives two cases: whichever status the woman had first decides the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was first his mother-in-law and then became a married woman, he is judged for his mother-in-law. If she was first a married woman and then became his mother-in-law, he is judged for a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with two mirror-image cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same woman can be forbidden for two reasons, and the order decides. If she became his mother-in-law first, he gets the punishment for a mother-in-law, burning. If she was married to another man first, he gets the punishment for a married woman, strangulation, even though burning is more severe.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, what counts is which prohibition came first, not which punishment is more severe.
steps.confusionAlert: In the second case רבי יוסי gives the lighter punishment (strangulation), because the married-woman prohibition came first. Severity does not decide for him.

phrases.english: His mother-in-law who then became a married woman –
he is sentenced for his mother-in-law.
A married woman who then became his mother-in-law –
he is sentenced for a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמוֹתוֹ וְנַעֲשֵׂית אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with examples.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The status the woman had first decides which death penalty is given.

steps.title: Mother-in-law who later became a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks רבא: if a woman was first his mother-in-law and later married someone else, is he judged only for the mother-in-law prohibition?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: His mother-in-law who later became a married woman — is he judged only for being with his mother-in-law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה takes one of the ברייתא's cases and asks רבא about it. This question sets up the challenge in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יוסי, the first status decides the punishment. Here she was his חמותו first and only later became an אשת איש. So by that rule he should be judged only for חמותו, and רב אדא is about to question that.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
His mother-in-law who then became a married woman,
is he judged only for his mother-in-law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא's rule that the first status decides, and applies it to a specific case in order to question it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in the case of a mother-in-law who later married, he is really judged only for the mother-in-law prohibition.

steps.title: He should also be judged for the married-woman prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא argues that he should also be judged for אשת איש, because רבי אבהו said רבי יוסי agrees when the second prohibition is an איסור מוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him also be judged for the prohibition of a married woman! For רבי אבהו said: רבי יוסי agrees in a case of an added prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא challenges the rule. He says the married-woman prohibition should also apply, and he uses a known statement of רבי אבהו as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually רבי יוסי holds that a second prohibition does not take hold on top of a first one. But רבי אבהו taught that רבי יוסי agrees when the second prohibition is wider and forbids her to more people. אשת איש forbids her to everyone, not just to her sons-in-law, so it should take hold here too.

keyTerms.meaning: an added prohibition, one that forbids the woman to more people than before

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוסי changed his mind in general. He still holds a second prohibition doesn't usually take hold. He only agrees when the second one is an איסור מוסיף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יוסי's 'first prohibition' rule has a known exception. The גמרא must now explain how the ברייתא's ruling fits with that exception, and the answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Let him be judged also for the prohibition of a married woman!
For Rabbi Abahu said:
Rabbi Yosei agrees in a case of an added prohibition.
phrases.notes: A married woman is forbidden to everyone, not just to her sons-in-law. So this second prohibition reaches more people.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִידּוֹן נָמֵי אַאִיסּוּר אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of the previous step into a full challenge, backed by רבי אבהו's principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling, by רבי יוסי, that the mother-in-law who later married is judged only as his mother-in-law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי agrees that an איסור מוסיף takes hold even on top of an existing prohibition. אשת איש is an added prohibition compared to חמותו. So the married-woman prohibition should also apply, and he should be judged for it as well.
